posts.title: OWE THE IRS? WHAT TO DO FIRST
posts.caption:
Owing the IRS feels like the walls are closing in. They aren't.
There's an order to fixing this, and most people get it backwards. File first. Know your real number. Then pick the option that fits your life, not the one a late-night ad sold you.
Save this. Send it to someone who's been avoiding the mailbox.
Let's talk: (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSHelp #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: CP2000 IS NOT AN AUDIT
posts.caption:
A CP2000 shows up and people assume they're being audited. They're not.
A computer compared your return to your 1099s and found a mismatch. That's it. And it's often wrong, especially on stock sales where it ignores what you paid.
Don't ignore it. Don't just pay it either. Check the math.
Questions about a notice? (813) 229-7100
#CP2000 #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: THE IRS 10-YEAR CLOCK
posts.caption:
The IRS has a deadline too. Most people never find out what theirs is.
Ten years from assessment, then the debt expires. But certain filings pause that clock, and the wrong one can hand the IRS years it didn't have.
Know your date before you choose a strategy.
Let's look at your transcripts: (813) 229-7100
#IRSHelp #TaxDebt #CSED

posts.title: CAN THE IRS TAKE YOUR PASSPORT?
posts.caption:
Yes. If you owe more than $66,000 (2026 figure, including penalties and interest) and the IRS has filed a lien or levied, it can certify you to the State Department.
The good news: a payment plan, an accepted offer, or hardship status keeps you off the list or gets you off it.
Trip coming up? Don't wait on this one. (813) 229-7100
#IRSHelp #PassportRevocation #TaxDebt

posts.title: OFFER IN COMPROMISE: MYTHS VS. FACTS
posts.caption:
"Pennies on the dollar" is a sales pitch, not a program.
An Offer in Compromise works when the IRS formula says you can't pay. When it doesn't, the fee and the down payment are usually gone. Run the numbers before anyone takes your money.
Want to know if you'd qualify? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#OfferInCompromise #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: HOW TO SET UP AN IRS PAYMENT PLAN
posts.caption:
Owing the IRS is stressful. A payment plan turns it into one monthly number.
There are four types: guaranteed, streamlined, non-streamlined and partial-pay. You can often apply online, and direct debit is the cheapest and safest way to pay.
Just know that penalties and interest keep running until the balance is gone, and a missed payment can put you in default.
Not sure which plan fits? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSPaymentPlan #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: PAYROLL TAX IS DIFFERENT
posts.caption:
Behind on payroll tax? Handle it first. Everything else can wait.
That money was withheld from your employees' paychecks. The IRS treats it like money held in trust, and the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty can reach responsible people personally, even with an LLC.
Get current on deposits, stop borrowing from payroll, and act early.
Talk it through before it escalates: (813) 229-7100
#PayrollTax #SmallBusiness #TaxDebt

posts.title: IRS TOOK YOUR REFUND? INJURED SPOUSE RELIEF
posts.caption:
The IRS kept your entire joint refund for your spouse's separate debt. You may be able to claim your share back.
It's Form 8379, and it's not the same as innocent spouse relief (Form 8857). One recovers a refund. The other releases you from a tax debt.
Don't wait. Filing alone has a time limit.
Questions about an offset? (813) 229-7100
#InjuredSpouse #Form8379 #IRSHelp

posts.title: HAVEN'T FILED IN YEARS? READ THIS
posts.caption:
Unfiled returns feel like a hole you can't climb out of. You can.
File even if you can't pay. Start with the last six years. Do it before the IRS files a Substitute for Return for you, because that version gives you no deductions at all.
Compliance comes first. Then we deal with the balance.
Let's get you caught up: (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#UnfiledTaxReturns #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: BEING AUDITED BY THE IRS?
posts.caption:
An audit letter is scary. Most audits are narrower than you think.
Answer only what's asked. Bring only what's requested. Stay truthful, and remember you can be represented. If you disagree with the result, IRS Appeals is still on the table.
Organized records are your best defense in an audit.
Before you say a word to the IRS: (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #TaxTips #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: STOP AN IRS WAGE GARNISHMENT
posts.caption:
A wage levy takes part of every paycheck until it's released. It doesn't stop on its own.
The good news: it can be released. An installment agreement, hardship status, an offer, or proof of economic hardship can get it done. File any missing returns first, because the IRS usually wants those in before it moves.
Don't let three paychecks vanish while you decide.
Garnishment questions? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSWageLevy #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: MOVED ABROAD AND STOPPED FILING?
posts.caption:
Moving overseas didn't end your U.S. tax filing obligation. It surprises a lot of people.
The tax itself is often small once the return is done right. The real danger is the forms you didn't know about, like the FBAR, and their penalties.
There's a program built for catching up. Coming forward beats getting found.
Living abroad and behind? (813) 229-7100
#ExpatTaxes #FBAR #IRSHelp

posts.title: SOMEONE FILED A RETURN IN YOUR NAME
posts.caption:
Your e-file got rejected, or the IRS wrote about a return you never filed. That's tax identity theft.
It's fixable and it's not your fault. File on paper with Form 14039, answer every IRS letter, and get an Identity Protection PIN.
It's slow. Start early.
Need help with an IRS notice? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IdentityTheft #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: GET IRS PENALTIES REMOVED
posts.caption:
Penalties are often the biggest chunk of an IRS balance, and the most negotiable.
There are two paths: First Time Abatement and Reasonable Cause. The IRS won't offer the first one. You have to ask.
Check your penalties before you negotiate anything else.
Want us to look at your transcripts? (813) 229-7100
#PenaltyAbatement #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: TAX LIENS: WHAT THEY DO
posts.caption:
A federal tax lien is a public claim against your property. It's a warning sign, not a seizure.
But it can block a sale or refinance and follow you into business deals. Release, discharge, subordination and withdrawal all do different things.
Know which one fits.
Talk through your lien: (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#TaxLien #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE IRS FROZE YOUR BANK ACCOUNT
posts.caption:
A bank levy is the IRS actually taking your money, not just claiming it.
Your bank freezes the funds and holds them for 21 days. After that, the money goes to the IRS and getting it back is extremely difficult. That 21-day window is where levies get released.
Save this. Send it to someone who just got a frozen-account surprise.
Need it handled fast? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#BankLevy #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: INNOCENT SPOUSE RELIEF
posts.caption:
Sign a joint return and you're both on the hook for the whole bill. Even when the mistake was only your spouse's.
Innocent spouse relief exists for exactly this. It's fact-heavy, the IRS scrutinizes it, and the deadlines matter.
If a joint return is coming back to haunt you, don't assume you have to pay it.
Questions? (813) 229-7100
#InnocentSpouse #IRSHelp #TaxTips

posts.title: CURRENTLY NOT COLLECTIBLE
posts.caption:
If you truly can't pay, the IRS has a pause button. It's called Currently Not Collectible.
Collection stops, but interest and penalties keep growing and the 10-year clock keeps running. It's a pause, not a pardon.
Know whether it fits before you pick an option.
Let's look at your situation: (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#CurrentlyNotCollectible #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: CRYPTO TAXES
posts.caption:
Trading one coin for another is a taxable event. You never have to touch a dollar for it to count.
Brokers now report to the IRS on Form 1099-DA, so the IRS will see more than it used to. Lost records and unfiled years are fixable. Ignoring them is not.
Get ahead of it before a notice arrives.
Talk it through: (813) 229-7100
#CryptoTaxes #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: IRS FRESH START: MYTHS VS. FACTS
posts.caption:
The Fresh Start Program is real. The "enrollment" being sold on TV is not.
There's no single application. It's a name for three IRS tools, and you apply for each one separately. Watch for the red flags before you hand anyone a check.
Not sure what fits? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#FreshStart #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: IRS CP14: YOUR FIRST BILL
posts.caption:
A CP14 is the IRS's first balance-due notice. It's polite, and it's your cheapest moment to act.
Check the tax year, the amount and the due date against your return. If you agree, pay. If you already paid, pull the records. If you can't pay, ask about a plan.
Don't let it turn into the second and third notice.
Questions about a notice? (813) 229-7100
#CP14 #IRSNotice #IRSHelp

posts.title: THE IRS NOTICE LADDER
posts.caption:
CP14, CP501, CP503, CP504, then a final notice. They are not all just bills.
Each step is closer to enforcement, and each one can reduce your options. The balance grows the whole way.
Know which rung you're on.
Got one in the mail? (813) 229-7100
#IRSNotice #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: FINAL NOTICE BEFORE LEVY
posts.caption:
Letter 1058, LT11 and CP90 are final notices of intent to levy.
They also give you Collection Due Process hearing rights. The request period is generally 30 days, so find the last date on your notice and act on it. A phone call is not a hearing request.
Call before the clock runs out: (813) 229-7100
#IRSLevy #CDPHearing #IRSHelp

posts.title: THE 90-DAY LETTER
posts.caption:
Letter 3219 is a Statutory Notice of Deficiency. It gives you 90 days to petition Tax Court.
The clock starts on the notice date, not the day you opened it. Calling the IRS doesn't stop it. Tax Court lets you dispute the tax before paying it.
You can settle later. You can't un-miss a deadline. (813) 229-7100
#TaxCourt #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: CP523: INTENT TO TERMINATE YOUR PAYMENT PLAN
posts.caption:
CP523 means the IRS says you defaulted on your installment agreement and intends to end it.
Find out why, contact the IRS within the window on your notice, and get reinstatement confirmed in writing. If the payment no longer fits, say so early.
Need help with a CP523? (813) 229-7100
#CP523 #InstallmentAgreement #IRSHelp

posts.title: LETTER 12C: THE IRS NEEDS MORE FROM YOU
posts.caption:
A Letter 12C means the IRS got your return but can't finish processing it.
It's a documentation request, and usually an easy one to fix. Send everything on the list, the first time, to the address on the letter. Skip the amended return.
Save this for when the envelope shows up.
Not sure what they're asking for? (813) 229-7100
#IRSLetter #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: MATH ERROR NOTICES: CHANGED WITHOUT AN AUDIT
posts.caption:
The IRS can change your return without auditing you. It's called a math error notice.
You don't get the usual audit steps first, but you do have 60 days to ask the IRS to reverse the change. Miss that window and your options get harder.
Check the correction. Respond in writing if it's wrong.
Questions about a notice? (813) 229-7100
#MathError #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: STUCK REFUND? IDENTITY VERIFICATION LETTERS
posts.caption:
If the IRS sent a 5071C, 4883C or 5747C, your refund is on hold until you verify.
Use the route on your letter, gather your papers first, and go to IRS.gov yourself. If you didn't file the return, say so during verification.
Waiting won't release it. Verifying will.
Need help with a letter? (813) 229-7100
#IRSRefund #IdentityVerification #IRSHelp

posts.title: CP59: THE IRS SAYS YOU DIDN'T FILE
posts.caption:
CP59 means the IRS has no record of your return. Silence afterward is not safety.
If you don't respond, the IRS may determine your tax for you, without your deductions. Already filed? Check the notice and send a copy. Haven't filed? File now, even if you can't pay.
Don't assume you owe. Many people are due money back.
Unfiled returns? (813) 229-7100
#CP59 #UnfiledTaxReturns #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: JANUARY 15 ESTIMATED TAX PAYMENT
posts.caption:
Self-employed or have 1099 income? The fourth estimated payment for 2026 is due Friday, January 15, 2027.
The penalty is figured one payment at a time, so April is too late to fix a missed January. Know your safe harbor number before you pay.
Do the math now.
Questions about estimated tax? (813) 229-7100
#EstimatedTax #SelfEmployedTax #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: 5 MISTAKES WITH IRS LETTERS
posts.caption:
Agreeing without checking. Sending half the documents. Calling when you should write. Missing a legal deadline. Not keeping copies.
Any one of them can turn a simple letter into a long fight.
Save this before the next envelope arrives.
Talk it through: (813) 229-7100
#IRSLetters #IRSHelp #TaxTips

posts.title: BEFORE YOU SIGN THAT IRS CERTIFIED LETTER
posts.caption:
Not every IRS letter is a threat. A certified one usually means enforcement is about to begin.
It often points to a levy or a lien, and it can start your 30 day window to request a collection due process hearing. That window is about timing, not forgiveness.
Read the date first. Then decide what to do.
Got one? Call (813) 229-7100 or visit getirshelp.com
#IRSHelp #IRSLetter #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: GET AN IP PIN BEFORE YOU FILE
posts.caption:
An IP PIN is a six-digit code that stops someone else from filing a return with your Social Security number.
You do not have to be an identity theft victim to get one. You can opt in through your IRS online account, and you need a new PIN every year.
Set it up before you file.
Identity theft questions? (813) 229-7100
#IPPIN #IdentityTheft #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: HOW TO READ YOUR IRS ACCOUNT TRANSCRIPT
posts.caption:
Your IRS letter is the summary. Your account transcript is the story.
Learn a few transaction codes and you can see what the IRS recorded: returns, assessments, refunds, holds. Match the codes to the events in your letter.
Save this for the next time one shows up.
Want help reading yours? (813) 229-7100
#IRSTranscript #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: IRS AUDIT RED FLAGS
posts.caption:
Audits aren't random anymore. Data matching looks for numbers that don't tell a believable story.
Think income that doesn't fit your lifestyle, round-number estimates, missing 1099s, aggressive Schedule C deductions and unreported crypto.
Real records and real numbers give you something to stand on.
Questions about an IRS letter? (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #TaxTips #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE BUSINESS STRUCTURE TRAP
posts.caption:
Your CPA sees structure as a way to file. The IRS sees it as a way to enforce.
Mixed finances, one entity doing everything and thin capital can make an audit spread. And on payroll tax, an LLC doesn't stop the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty.
Look at your setup before the IRS does.
Talk it through: (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#PayrollTax #SmallBusinessTax #IRSHelp

posts.title: WHEN YOU NEED A TAX ATTORNEY, NOT A CPA
posts.caption:
CPAs focus on accuracy. Tax attorneys focus on advocacy. You may need both, just not at the same time.
Attorney-client privilege, Tax Court petitions and the chance of a criminal tax issue are the moments an attorney matters most.
Save this and send it to a business owner you know.
Free call: (813) 229-7100
#TaxAttorney #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: DO YOU ACTUALLY QUALIFY FOR IRS DEBT RELIEF?
posts.caption:
Owing the IRS doesn't mean you qualify for relief. Everything runs on ability to pay.
The IRS uses its own formula and its own expense schedule, not your real budget. Apply before you know your numbers and a denial can hand them your whole financial picture.
Ask what your best outcome is, not what you qualify for.
Want your numbers run first? (813) 229-7100
#IRSHelp #OfferInCompromise #TaxDebt

posts.title: CHOOSING A TAX PREPARER
posts.caption:
Most preparers do the work right. These are the basic rules every paid preparer has to follow.
Sign the return. Show a PTIN. Hand you a copy before you sign. Never cash your refund check.
If you hear something else, walk away.
Need a second set of eyes? (813) 229-7100
#TaxPreparer #TaxSeason #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: WHEN YOUR SPOUSE OWES THE IRS
posts.caption:
Marriage alone doesn't make their tax debt yours. How your finances connect to theirs is what creates the risk.
Joint returns, shared accounts, jointly titled property and community property rules can all pull you in. Separate, documented finances protect you. Good intentions don't.
Questions about your exposure? (813) 229-7100
#IRSHelp #TaxAttorney #SpouseTaxDebt

posts.title: THE IRS APPEALS PROCESS
posts.caption:
Disagree with the IRS? Appeals is independent of the examiner and built to settle disputes without court.
Answer the 30-day letter with a written protest, or use Form 12203 on smaller cases. It covers levies, liens and rejected payment plans too.
Got a letter you disagree with? (813) 229-7100
#IRSAppeals #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: THE REAL COST OF WAITING UNTIL APRIL
posts.caption:
April is when you report the past. Planning is what you do before the year closes.
Entity decisions, retirement contributions and income timing can slip away quietly. Nobody sends a reminder.
Start the conversation while you still have choices: (813) 229-7100
#TaxPlanning #SmallBusinessTaxes #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: SELLING A HOME WITH AN IRS LIEN
posts.caption:
A federal tax lien on title doesn't automatically kill the sale.
A Certificate of Discharge can clear the lien from the one property you're selling, and the IRS is often owed far less than the lien's face amount. The catch is timing, so start early.
Closing coming up? Call (813) 229-7100
#IRSLien #SellingYourHome #TaxLien

posts.title: CP2501: THE WARNING BEFORE CP2000
posts.caption:
A CP2501 says the income the IRS received doesn't match your return. It isn't a bill.
But it does need an answer. Ignore it and the case can move to a CP2000, then a statutory notice of deficiency.
Agree, disagree, or need more time: reply before the date on the notice.
Got one? (813) 229-7100
#CP2501 #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: MATCH EVERY 1099 BEFORE YOU FILE
posts.caption:
The IRS already has copies of your W-2s and 1099s. A return that does not match gets noticed.
Check stock basis, crypto on the new 1099-DA, and payment app income before you file, not after a CP2000.
Compare your pile to the IRS's copy first.
Got a mismatch notice? (813) 229-7100
#CP2000 #TaxSeason #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE 90-DAY LETTER (CP3219A)
posts.caption:
A CP3219A is a statutory notice of deficiency. It gives you the chance to go to Tax Court before paying the disputed amount.
The period is generally 90 days. Writing to the IRS does not extend it.
Find the date on your notice and protect it first.
Holding one of these? (813) 229-7100
#CP3219A #TaxCourt #IRSHelp

posts.title: THE MISTAKE THAT MAKES IRS AUDITS WORSE
posts.caption:
Audits rarely go wrong because someone cheated. They go wrong because of how the taxpayer responds.
Too much talking. Too much sharing. Signing a report just to make it stop.
Records can often be rebuilt, and the first auditor's report is not a verdict.
Facing an audit? Call (813) 229-7100 or visit getirshelp.com
#IRSAudit #TaxAttorney #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE IRS CHANGED YOUR RETURN (CP22A)
posts.caption:
A CP22A means the IRS changed your return and now there's a balance due.
Don't pay it blindly. Don't ignore it. Compare each change to what you filed, then pay it or dispute it in writing.
Not sure which? (813) 229-7100
#CP22A #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: ACCOUNT ADJUSTED (CP21A)
posts.caption:
A CP21A means the IRS adjusted your tax account and you may owe.
Sometimes it's just your amended return showing up. Sometimes it's a removed credit or a surprise penalty.
Verify before you pay.
Questions about an adjustment? (813) 229-7100
#CP21A #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE HOME SALE EXCLUSION TRAPS
posts.caption:
Up to $250,000 (single) or $500,000 (joint) of home sale gain can be excluded. Only if you pass the tests.
Rental time, depreciation and a 1099-S you forgot to report can all bite. A CP2000 is the usual result of skipping the reporting.
Check the tests before closing, not after the notice.
Questions about a sale? (813) 229-7100
#HomeSale #TaxAttorney #IRSHelp

posts.title: WHY REFUNDS GET HELD
posts.caption:
A late refund does not always mean a mistake.
By law, refunds with the Earned Income Credit or refundable child tax credit cannot go out before February 15. Old debts can take a refund. Identity checks can freeze one.
Read the letter before you panic.
Refund stuck? (813) 229-7100
#TaxRefund #IRSLetter #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: YOUR RETURN IS UNDER REVIEW
posts.caption:
CP05 or Letter 4464C: the IRS is holding your refund while it reviews your return.
That is not an audit. Usually you wait about 60 days. If a CP05A follows, respond fully and by the date shown.
Skip the second return and the weekly calls.
Refund stuck? (813) 229-7100
#IRSRefund #CP05 #TaxTips

posts.title: S CORP ELECTION AND REASONABLE PAY
posts.caption:
An S corp election can make sense for the right business. The salary is where owners get hurt.
You become an employee of your own company, and it has to pay you a reasonable wage through payroll. Taking only distributions is the most common mistake.
Document the number before payroll starts.
Planning an election? (813) 229-7100
#SCorp #SmallBusinessTax #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: MARCH 15 BUSINESS RETURNS
posts.caption:
Partnership and S corporation returns are due March 15, a month before your personal return.
The late penalty is charged per owner, per month, and it does not depend on tax owed. Form 7004 gets six more months to file.
Put it on the calendar now.
Business tax questions? (813) 229-7100
#SCorp #Partnership #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: REFUND HELD FOR UNFILED RETURNS (CP63)
posts.caption:
The IRS is holding your refund because it shows returns you haven't filed.
File them, or explain why you didn't have to or already did. Wait too long and the IRS may file for you.
A return you prepare beats one the IRS prepares.
Need help catching up? (813) 229-7100
#CP63 #UnfiledReturns #IRSHelp

posts.title: REFUND APPLIED TO A BALANCE (CP49)
posts.caption:
Your refund didn't arrive because the IRS applied it to a balance from another year.
The offset is automatic. The balance behind it might be wrong. Check that year first.
Joint return? You may be an injured spouse.
Want the debt resolved? (813) 229-7100
#CP49 #IRSRefund #TaxDebt

posts.title: LAWYERS WHO HAVEN'T FILED: DARRIN'S VIEW
posts.caption:
A skipped year makes the next one harder. It's a trap, not a character flaw.
Silence feels safe, but a year you never filed has no IRS clock running on it, and the IRS can file a substitute return for you.
In Darrin's view, filing before the IRS comes knocking is what keeps this a civil problem.
Lawyer to lawyer: (813) 229-7100
#UnfiledTaxes #TaxAttorney #IRSHelp

posts.title: THE ESTIMATED TAX PENALTY (CP30)
posts.caption:
The CP30 is a penalty for not paying enough tax during the year.
It's figured quarter by quarter, and there are safe harbors that avoid it. Form 2210 can reduce or remove it in the right situations.
Check the quarters before you pay.
Questions? (813) 229-7100
#CP30 #EstimatedTax #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: YOUR PAYMENT WAS MOVED (CP60)
posts.caption:
CP60 means the IRS removed a payment it had applied to your account in error.
If the payment was yours, prove it with a bank statement, cancelled check or confirmation number. If it wasn't, the balance is real.
Either way, move quickly.
Need a hand? (813) 229-7100
#CP60 #IRSNotice #TaxTips

posts.title: THE BUYER DTI TRAP
posts.caption:
Your IRS payment plan counts as monthly debt when a lender runs your mortgage numbers.
On a tight file, a $500 payment can be the difference between approved and denied. There are ways that may free up room, and an offer can take 6 to 12 months.
Raise it at pre-qualification, while there's time.
Buying a home with an IRS plan? (813) 229-7100
#MortgageTips #IRSPaymentPlan #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: CREDITS ON FILE, NO RETURN (CP80)
posts.caption:
The IRS may be holding your estimated payments or withholding for a year you never filed.
You generally have three years from the original due date to claim a refund. After that, the credit generally can't be refunded.
File before the clock runs out.
Need help filing? (813) 229-7100
#CP80 #IRSRefund #UnfiledReturns

posts.title: THE AUGUSTA RULE
posts.caption:
Rent your home to your business for fewer than 15 days a year and the rent may be tax free to you and deductible to the company.
That is real law. It only holds up with comparable rates, a signed agreement, and minutes for every meeting.
No paperwork, no rule.
Thinking about it? (813) 229-7100
#AugustaRule #BusinessOwner #TaxPlanning

posts.title: OWE MORE THAN EXPECTED
posts.caption:
You finished your return and the balance due is bigger than you planned.
File on time anyway. Pay what you can by April 15. Then ask about a payment plan for the rest.
A bill you can see is easier to handle than one you ignore.
Want a plan? (813) 229-7100
#TaxDebt #PaymentPlan #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: AUDIT 30-DAY LETTER: YOUR CHOICES
posts.caption:
An audit 30-day letter is the IRS saying what it proposes to change.
You can agree, agree in part, or protest. The right call comes from your records and the law, not from nerves.
Just know that if the 30 days pass, the next letter has a Tax Court clock.
Got a 30-day letter? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSAudit #TaxAttorney #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: LETTER 566: THE IRS WANTS YOUR DOCUMENTS
posts.caption:
Letter 566 means your return was picked for an audit. It does not mean you did something wrong.
Send copies, never originals. Put your name and Social Security number on each page. Ask for more time before the due date, not after.
Stay silent and the IRS disallows the items.
Need help with the response? (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #Letter566 #TaxHelp

posts.title: CAN'T PAY? FILE ANYWAY
posts.caption:
Not filing costs 5% of the unpaid tax per month. Not paying costs 0.5%.
That is why the advice is always the same: file by the deadline, even if you cannot pay. You can work out the payment after.
File first.
Behind on filing or paying? (813) 229-7100
#FileAnyway #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: TAX FRAUD VICTIM? DO THIS FIRST
posts.caption:
Someone filed a return with your Social Security number. Don't panic. Follow the process.
File Form 14039, notify the IRS, FTC, credit bureaus and your bank, freeze your credit, and get an IP PIN.
Document everything. Never ignore an IRS letter.
Need help sorting it out? (813) 229-7100
#IdentityTheft #TaxFraud #IRSHelp

posts.title: LETTER 2205-A: YOUR FIRST AUDIT LETTER
posts.caption:
A revenue agent has been assigned to your return. Letter 2205-A lists the issues and asks you to call.
IRS procedures allow 14 calendar days. Sign Form 2848 first if you want someone else to handle the agent.
Ignoring the letter does not stop the audit.
Talk before you call the agent: (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #FieldAudit #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: AN EXTENSION IS NOT TIME TO PAY
posts.caption:
Form 4868 gives you until October 15 to file. It does not give you until October to pay.
Interest starts April 15 on anything unpaid. Pay what you can with the request.
Know the difference before you extend.
Questions? (813) 229-7100
#TaxExtension #Form4868 #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: OFFICE AUDIT APPOINTMENT LETTER
posts.caption:
Letter 725A sets your audit appointment at an IRS office.
Use the document list as your checklist. Organize by issue. With Form 2848 on file, a representative can attend for you.
Call to reschedule. Don't just skip it.
Audit coming up? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSAudit #OfficeAudit #TaxAttorney

posts.title: REFINANCING WITH AN IRS LIEN
posts.caption:
A federal tax lien can kill a refinance at the title search. Lenders won't fund behind the IRS.
Subordination moves the new loan ahead of the lien. The lien and the debt stay. Plan on 45 to 75 days and wait for the lender's commitment before filing.
Refinance stuck on a lien? (813) 229-7100
#TaxLien #Refinance #IRSHelp

posts.title: IRS LETTER 979: RECORDS NOT ADEQUATE
posts.caption:
Letter 979 is not a bill. It does not reopen the audit years or add tax by itself.
It puts a finding in your file, and the real risk is the next audit. Respond in writing with the recordkeeping system you actually have in place.
Got a 979? Have us review the response first: (813) 229-7100
#Letter979 #IRSAudit #SmallBusinessTax

posts.title: HIRING YOUR CHILD
posts.caption:
Putting your child on the payroll can work. It works only if the job is real and the pay is fair.
Your entity type changes the payroll tax result, and the timesheet is what carries the deduction.
Chores do not count.
Questions before you start? (813) 229-7100
#FamilyBusiness #TaxPlanning #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: LETTER 907: IRS WANTS MORE TIME TO ASSESS
posts.caption:
Letter 907 comes with Form 872, a request to extend the three-year assessment deadline.
Your signature is required, so you have options. You can limit the extension or refuse it, and a fixed date beats an open-ended consent.
Call before you sign: (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #Form872 #TaxAttorney

posts.title: FOUND A MISTAKE AFTER FILING
posts.caption:
You filed, then spotted an error. Do not panic, and do not guess.
Form 1040-X fixes a return, but some problems are fixed by answering an IRS notice instead. Refund claims have a deadline.
Fix it on your terms.
Need help deciding? (813) 229-7100
#AmendedReturn #Form1040X #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: LETTER 3172: THE IRS FILED A LIEN
posts.caption:
Letter 3172 isn't a warning. The lien is already on public record.
It also opens a hearing right. File Form 12153 by the date printed on the letter to raise a payment plan, an offer or hardship.
A lien hearing doesn't stop levies on its own, so watch for other notices too.
Call (813) 229-7100
#TaxLien #IRSLetter #CollectionDueProcess

posts.title: WHAT THE IRS WILL WATCH IN 2026
posts.caption:
Most business owners don't get in trouble because they're dishonest. They only think about taxes once a year.
The IRS already has your 1099s, W-2s and payment platform records. Round-number expenses and mixed accounts look like guesses.
Build monthly habits and act before the IRS contacts you.
Questions? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#SmallBusinessTaxes #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: CP75: THE IRS IS AUDITING YOUR EITC
posts.caption:
A CP75 asks you to prove the credit. Each child must meet the relationship, age and residency tests.
Send exactly what the notice asks for. A denial can lead to a ban from claiming the credit, and Form 8862 afterward.
EITC audit notice? (813) 229-7100
#EITC #CP75 #IRSAudit

posts.title: CP79 VS. CP79A: CREDIT BAN
posts.caption:
CP79 is a recertification requirement. CP79A is a two-year ban. Same credits, very different notices.
Form 8862 is how you claim the credits again, and audit reconsideration is there if you disagree.
Which one did you get? (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#IRSNotice #EITC #TaxAttorney

posts.title: AGENTS: SPOT IRS PROBLEMS EARLY
posts.caption:
Liens usually surface at the title search, after the contract is signed. Ask sellers and buyers the IRS question up front.
Match the procedure to the deal: discharge for a sale, subordination for a refinance, restructure a buyer's plan first. Our free 14-page field guide has the details.
Agents and title pros, call us: (813) 229-7100
#RealEstateAgent #TaxLien #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: SOMEONE ELSE CLAIMED YOUR DEPENDENT
posts.caption:
CP87A means another return used the same Social Security number for a dependent on yours.
The IRS says it is not auditing you and you don't need to send documents. Check the numbers, review the rules, and correct your return with Form 1040-X if you listed someone who doesn't qualify.
Dependent dispute? (813) 229-7100
#CP87A #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: ACCOUNTABLE PLAN
posts.caption:
An accountable plan lets your company repay your business costs without treating them as wages.
It works only if every expense is real, reported within 60 days, and any excess is returned within 120. Flat monthly amounts fail.
Get it in writing before the first reimbursement.
Let's set it up right: (813) 229-7100
#AccountablePlan #SmallBusinessTax #TaxTips

posts.title: CP71: THE ANNUAL BALANCE REMINDER
posts.caption:
The IRS sends a yearly reminder while your balance is open, even if your account is in hardship status.
Hardship isn't forgiveness. Interest keeps adding up.
Ignore it long enough and a lien or a private collection agency may be next.
Got one? Call (813) 229-7100
#CP71 #IRSNotice #TaxDebt

posts.title: THE IRS WANTS YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY
posts.caption:
A CP91 says the IRS intends to levy up to 15% of your Social Security benefits.
Calling Social Security won't stop it. The IRS is the only one who can. Raise hardship before the levy starts, not after.
Save this for someone on benefits.
Need help now? (813) 229-7100
#CP91 #SocialSecurity #IRSHelp

posts.title: WHY THE IRS TURNED DOWN A SETTLEMENT
posts.caption:
A federal appeals court backed the IRS in rejecting a taxpayer's offer. The IRS ran his numbers, found it could collect far more, and also cited public policy.
Your offer has to match the formula, not your story.
Honest debt you truly can't pay is what the program is for.
Before you file an offer: (813) 229-7100
#OfferInCompromise #IRSDebt #TaxAttorney

posts.title: FEDERAL CONTRACTORS: LEVY FIRST, HEARING AFTER
posts.caption:
For federal contractors, the IRS can levy first and offer the hearing after.
You have 30 days from the notice date to file Form 12153. A hearing request does not stop further levies.
Protect the deadline and work the balance at the same time.
Call (813) 229-7100
#FederalContractor #IRSLevy #CollectionDueProcess

posts.title: THE IRS MAY CONTACT OTHERS ABOUT YOU
posts.caption:
Before the IRS calls your employer or bank about your tax debt, it generally has to tell you first.
That notice is your window to hand over the information yourself. Unfiled returns? An LT41 means a Substitute for Return may be coming.
Get ahead of it: (813) 229-7100
#IRSNotice #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: THE IRS SHORT-TERM PAYMENT PLAN
posts.caption:
Up to 180 days to pay in full, with no setup fee. It is not an installment agreement.
Interest and penalties keep running, you get no installment appeal rights, and only one plan at a time. It works when the money has a date.
Not sure which plan fits? (813) 229-7100
#IRSPaymentPlan #TaxDebt #IRSHelp

posts.title: YOUR PAYMENT PLAN LETTER, DECODED
posts.caption:
LT23 is a warning. Letter 2975 means the agreement defaulted. 2975C follows a bankruptcy.
Same payment plan, very different letters. Check the number before you react, and fix the cause before the 30 days run out.
Questions? (813) 229-7100
#InstallmentAgreement #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: HOME OFFICE DEDUCTION
posts.caption:
Exclusive means exclusive. A guest bed or a family computer in the room can sink the deduction for the whole space.
If you own an S or C corporation, the rules are different, and an accountable plan may be the better route.
Take the photos before you rearrange anything.
Not sure your space qualifies? (813) 229-7100
#HomeOffice #SelfEmployed #TaxPlanning

posts.title: LETTER 2603C: PLAN APPROVED, LIEN FILED
posts.caption:
Your payment plan stops the levy. It does not stop the lien.
Letter 2603C tells you a Notice of Federal Tax Lien is coming with the agreement. There may be ways to avoid it or remove it later.
Talk before it hits the public record: (813) 229-7100
#TaxLien #InstallmentAgreement #IRSLetter

posts.title: WHEN THE IRS LEVIES PROPERTY THAT ISN'T THE TAXPAYER'S
posts.caption:
Joint account. Business account. Money held for someone else. If the IRS levied it, you may have a wrongful levy claim.
The claim clock is generally two years from the levy, and the suit deadline is separate. Letters 3973, 3974 and 3975 each change your next move.
Watch the dates: (813) 229-7100
#WrongfulLevy #IRSLevy #TaxAttorney

posts.title: NOT FILED IN 10+ YEARS? THE IRS HASN'T FORGOTTEN
posts.caption:
You're not invisible. The IRS has information returns, payment platform data and more.
Most nonfilers aren't criminals. They're overwhelmed.
Moving first keeps your options open. Waiting hands the IRS the lead.
Let's make a plan: (813) 229-7100
#UnfiledTaxes #IRSHelp #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: LETTER 4000: APPEALS' LAST OPPORTUNITY
posts.caption:
Letter 4000 means Appeals tried to reach you and is now giving you one more chance, generally 14 days.
Ignore it and Appeals decides on the file it already has. Need more time? Ask before the deadline passes.
Don't lose the hearing by silence.
Call (813) 229-7100
#Letter4000 #IRSAppeals #CollectionDueProcess

posts.title: THE IRS PREPARED YOUR RETURN FOR YOU
posts.caption:
A Substitute for Return only knows what third parties reported. No deductions beyond the standard one, no credits, no business expenses.
That is why your own return is usually the better number. File it before the assessment.
Let's get it filed: (813) 229-7100
#SFR #UnfiledReturns #IRSHelp

posts.title: OWE THE IRS OVER $50,000?
posts.caption:
You can still get a payment plan. You just get a deeper look at your finances.
Pay down to $50,000 or less and you may qualify for a Simple Payment Plan. Above that, expect managerial approval, a financial statement in many cases, and a lien decision.
Build your budget before the IRS builds it for you. (813) 229-7100
#TaxDebt #IRSPaymentPlan #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: REFUND CLAIM DENIED
posts.caption:
Letter 105C means the IRS denied your refund claim. Generally you have two years from the letter date to sue.
Appealing does not extend that clock. Only Form 907 does. Write the date down today.
Protect your claim: (813) 229-7100
#RefundClaim #IRSLetter #TaxAttorney

posts.title: SOLO 401(k) VS SEP-IRA
posts.caption:
Both plans can fund your retirement. They are not interchangeable.
A solo 401(k) has an election deadline that ends with the year. A SEP-IRA is easy to start, but it must cover eligible employees at the same percentage you take.
Count your staff first.
Comparing plans? (813) 229-7100
#Solo401k #SEPIRA #TaxPlanning

posts.title: CP161: YOUR BUSINESS OWES THE IRS
posts.caption:
A CP161 means the IRS shows an unpaid balance on a business or entity return.
Check the math against your return and the payments applied. If something looks wrong, contact the IRS within 10 days of the notice date.
Can't pay it all? Ask about a payment arrangement before the balance grows.
Questions about a notice? (813) 229-7100
#CP161 #BusinessTax #IRSNotice

posts.title: CP259: BUSINESS RETURN NOT FILED
posts.caption:
The IRS expected a business return and says it never got one.
Maybe it wasn't processed, maybe it went to the wrong address, maybe it slipped. Either way, a late partnership or S-corp return can carry a penalty even when no tax is due.
File first, then ask about penalty relief.
Let's sort it out: (813) 229-7100
#CP259 #BusinessTax #IRSHelp

posts.title: BUSINESS OWES BACK TAXES? WHAT THE IRS CAN DO NEXT
posts.caption:
It's not the balance. It's what the IRS is allowed to do.
Business accounts, receivables and payroll are common targets, and each ignored notice shifts your case.
Your options are widest before enforcement starts.
Call (813) 229-7100 or visit getirshelp.com
#BusinessTaxes #IRSDebt #TaxAttorney

posts.title: CP2100: B NOTICES FOR BUSINESSES
posts.caption:
CP2100 goes to the payer, not the payee. It lists payee TINs that are missing or don't match.
You send the B notice. You start backup withholding when the rules say so. Miss it and the business can owe what should have been withheld.
Keep the list, the notices and the mailing records.
Need help with compliance? (813) 229-7100
#CP2100 #BackupWithholding #SmallBusinessTax

posts.title: LETTER 1153: YOUR APPEAL WINDOW
posts.caption:
Letter 1153 proposes personal liability for unpaid payroll taxes. It also opens a protest window.
The letter generally gives you 60 days. Use the exact date printed on it. A focused protest tells the IRS about your actual role.
Call before the clock runs out: (813) 229-7100
#Letter1153 #TrustFundRecoveryPenalty #IRSHelp

posts.title: IRS REJECTED YOUR PAYMENT PLAN?
posts.caption:
A rejection isn't final. You can appeal through the Collection Appeals Program with Form 9423, and you have 30 days. No extensions.
Fix the problem, appeal, or change plans. Don't resend the same request unchanged.
Got a rejection letter? Call before day 30: (813) 229-7100
#IRSAppeal #IRSPaymentPlan #IRSHelp

posts.title: LETTER 3586: THE TFRP INTERVIEW
posts.caption:
The IRS wants a Form 4180 interview to decide who was responsible and whether the failure was willful.
Your answers become evidence. Know the records, stick to facts, and prepare before you sit down.
Don't go in alone: (813) 229-7100
#Letter3586 #TaxAttorney #IRSHelp

posts.title: HSA RULES FOR OWNERS
posts.caption:
An HSA can be deductible going in and tax free for medical costs coming out. The entry rules are strict.
You qualify month by month, and funding employee accounts triggers a comparability rule.
Keep every receipt.
Check your eligibility before you fund: (813) 229-7100
#HSA #SmallBusinessTax #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: CP297: BUSINESS LEVY NOTICE
posts.caption:
CP297 is the final notice of intent to levy against a business. It comes with Collection Due Process rights.
You have 30 days from the notice date to file Form 12153. Bank accounts, receivables and equipment are all at risk.
The deadline is real: (813) 229-7100
#CP297 #BusinessTax #IRSLevy

posts.title: OFFER REJECTED VS. RETURNED
posts.caption:
A rejected offer (Letter 686C) can be appealed within 30 days. A returned offer (Letter 4112C) can't, but you can fix it and resubmit.
Check the letter number before you do anything.
Not sure which you have? (813) 229-7100
#OfferInCompromise #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: IRS AUDITS AREN'T SCARY IF YOU KNOW THIS
posts.caption:
Find out why you were selected. Keep receipts, not just bank statements. Respond before the deadline.
You have the right to appeal and to representation. A notice of deficiency gives you 90 days to petition Tax Court.
Questions about an audit notice? (813) 229-7100
#IRSAudit #TaxTips #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: OFFER ACCEPTED: NOW WHAT?
posts.caption:
An accepted offer is a contract. Pay on schedule. File and pay on time for five years under the standard Form 656 terms.
Break the terms and the IRS can reinstate the unpaid balance of the original debt.
Keep every document. Questions? (813) 229-7100
#OfferInCompromise #IRSHelp #TaxRelief

posts.title: THE THREE IRS CRYPTO LETTERS
posts.caption:
Letter 6174 educates. Letter 6174-A suggests you may need to amend. Letter 6173 requires a response by the date at the top.
Know which one you hold, and don't sign a statement your records can't support.
Need help responding? (813) 229-7100
#CryptoTax #IRSLetter #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: MISSED AN IRS PAYMENT?
posts.caption:
Your plan doesn't vanish the day a payment is late. The IRS must send a CP523 and give at least 30 days' notice before terminating.
Cure the default within 45 days and the IRS must reinstate. Better still, ask to change the payment before you miss one.
Got a CP523? Call us: (813) 229-7100
#CP523 #IRSPaymentPlan #TaxDebt

posts.title: FRIVOLOUS RETURN POSITIONS
posts.caption:
Arguments like "wages aren't income" have been rejected. A frivolous return carries a $5,000 penalty under Code section 6702.
Letters 3175C and 3176C are warnings. Take them seriously and file an honest return.
Let's get you back on solid ground: (813) 229-7100
#FrivolousReturn #IRSHelp #TaxAttorney

posts.title: COST SEGREGATION
posts.caption:
A cost segregation study splits a building into parts that depreciate faster. A weak study can backfire.
It takes an engineer, workpapers, and a close look at your purchase contract and acquisition date.
Think engineering first, tax second.
Own or buying a building? (813) 229-7100
#CostSegregation #RealEstateInvestor #TaxPlanning

posts.title: HOW TO FIND YOUR IRS LETTER NUMBER
posts.caption:
Every IRS letter has a number. It is the most important thing on the page.
Look in the top or bottom right corner of page one. CP means computer. LTR means a specific IRS function or person. LT means collection.
Find it first. Then decide what to do.
Not sure what yours means? (813) 229-7100
#IRSLetter #IRSNotice #TaxHelp

posts.title: IRS NOTICE VS. LETTER
posts.caption:
They look the same. They are not the same.
A CP notice is automated. An LTR letter often means an active case with a person behind it. Your response should match.
Know whether you are dealing with a machine or a person.
Questions about a letter? (813) 229-7100
#IRSNotice #IRSLetter #TaxTips

posts.title: SHORT SALE TAX TRAP
posts.caption:
The short sale closes. Then a 1099-C arrives and the forgiven debt looks like income.
Exclusions such as qualified principal residence debt or insolvency may apply, but you have to claim them on Form 982.
Talk to a tax professional before you file that year's return. (813) 229-7100
#ShortSale #1099C #TaxAttorney

posts.title: GOT AN IRS LETTER? DO THIS FIRST
posts.caption:
An IRS letter is a signal, not a verdict. But the first day matters.
Open it. Find the number. Find the deadline. Read every word. Copy it. Calendar it.
And resist the urge to overshare or rush.
Want a second set of eyes? (813) 229-7100
#IRSHelp #IRSLetter #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: IRS DEADLINES YOU CANNOT MISS
posts.caption:
The clock starts on the date printed on the letter, not the day you open it.
Final levy notices, 30-day audit letters, notices of deficiency and CP523 each have their own window. Miss one and you lose options.
Calendar it the day it arrives.
Have a letter in hand? (813) 229-7100
#IRSDeadlines #IRSNotice #TaxHelp

posts.title: THE PARTIAL PAYMENT PLAN
posts.caption:
A PPIA lets you pay what you can afford. What's left can expire at the collection deadline.
The trade: a full financial review, a check-in every two years, and penalties and interest that keep growing.
Wondering if it fits? (813) 229-7100
#PPIA #IRSPaymentPlan #TaxAttorney

posts.title: IRS LETTERS FOR BUSINESS OWNERS
posts.caption:
Business owners get a wider range of IRS letters, with higher penalties and tighter deadlines.
Payroll notices, late return penalties, non-filer notices and B-notices each need a different response.
Read the identifier closely before you answer.
Got a business letter? (813) 229-7100
#BusinessTax #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: 1031 EXCHANGE
posts.caption:
A 1031 exchange can defer tax on investment real estate. It has to be set up before you close.
Forty-five days to identify, 180 days to finish, and a qualified intermediary holding the money. Never backdate a letter.
Call before you list the property.
Planning a sale? (813) 229-7100
#1031Exchange #RealEstateInvestor #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: IRS LETTER 6201
posts.caption:
Letter 6201 is the IRS tax compliance report. Lenders and employers sometimes ask for it.
Even an installment agreement can show up as a compliance issue. Share the original authenticated PDF, not a screenshot.
Fix the cause, not the label.
Need help with a filing or payment issue? (813) 229-7100
#Letter6201 #IRSHelp #TaxCompliance

posts.title: CAN THE IRS LEVY WITHOUT NOTICE?
posts.caption:
Generally, no. The IRS must send a final notice of intent to levy at least 30 days before it levies.
There are exceptions, and a CP504 can still let the IRS take a state refund. If a levy hits your bank, you have 21 days before the funds go to the IRS.
Know the rules before you need them.
Facing a levy notice? (813) 229-7100
#IRSLevy #TaxDebt #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: TAX LIENS ON ESTATE SALES
posts.caption:
A tax lien doesn't disappear when the owner dies.
Income tax liens and, on larger estates, the automatic estate tax lien can both cloud title. Distribution to heirs doesn't cure either one.
Plan for a longer closing timeline. (813) 229-7100 or getirshelp.com
#EstateSale #TaxLien #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: OFFER IN COMPROMISE LETTERS
posts.caption:
An offer in compromise generates a letter at every stage.
Returned is not rejected. Rejected means 30 days to appeal. Accepted means five years of compliance.
Every letter in the sequence matters.
Thinking about an offer? (813) 229-7100
#OfferInCompromise #IRSHelp #TaxDebt

posts.title: THE IRS NON-FILER LETTER SEQUENCE
posts.caption:
The IRS sends several notices before it prepares a return for you.
CP59, CP516, CP518, then a CP2566 Substitute for Return. The one they file for you gives you the standard deduction and nothing more.
Take the first chance and file your own.
Behind on returns? (813) 229-7100
#UnfiledTaxes #IRSNotice #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: OFFER IN COMPROMISE OR PAYMENT PLAN?
posts.caption:
If you can pay in full over time, the IRS generally won't take an offer. That's the dividing line.
Offer payments are generally kept even if the offer is rejected, so run the numbers first.
Get your numbers reviewed: (813) 229-7100
#OfferInCompromise #IRSPaymentPlan #TampaTaxAttorney

posts.title: LETTERS AFTER IDENTITY THEFT
posts.caption:
CP01S is a receipt. CP01 means your claim was verified. CP01A gives you an IP PIN for the filing season.
And CP566 and CP567? Those are ITIN notices, not identity theft.
Check the number, then match it to your records.
Questions about your case? (813) 229-7100
#IdentityTheft #IPPIN #IRSHelp

posts.title: CHARITABLE GIVING AND THE PAPER TRAIL
posts.caption:
Direct gifts, donor advised funds, and IRA transfers each have their own rules. So does the proof.
One missing sentence in a charity's letter cost a couple their deduction in Tax Court. New rules also start with 2026 tax years.
Keep the letter.
Planning your giving? (813) 229-7100
#CharitableGiving #DAF #TaxPlanning
